**Why M2:**
- **The loop has no source of ΔV.** M1 and M2 are the same size, Q1 and Q2 have no area ratio, and the M3/M4 mirror is 1:1. With everything matched, the only solution that satisfies the loop is I·R1 ≈ 0. That means the core either has no stable non-zero operating point or only a very weak one.
- **That fits the failed start-up.** With no proper operating point, the core cannot settle into a self-sustaining bias, so `startup_ok` = 0.
- **It also fits the bad line regulation.** Whatever current is flowing appears to be held up by the start-up path (Mst1/Mst3 sinking current from node g), not by the core's own feedback. That current tracks VDD, which would give the 0.113 V/V line regulation and poor PSRR. VREF still lands near 0.64 V only because Vbe(Q3) plus a small I·R2 happens to fall inside the window.

**Alternatives, in order:**
- **M1:** shrunk to the same width as M2, which removes the size ratio in the same way.
- **Mst2:** a start-up device fault that leaves Mst3 conducting during normal operation would also hurt line regulation. It is less likely because it doesn't explain the missing ratio in the core.

This is reasoned from the netlist and the spec results only. I didn't run any simulations.
